questions.question_text: Simethicone is a component of several antacid formulations. Chemically it is
questions.explanation: Simethicone is a mixture of simethicone containing polydimethylsiloxane and silica.

questions.question_text: The pharmacy Council of India is constituted by the
questions.explanation: The Pharmacy Council of India (PCI) is constituted by the Central Government under Section 3 of the Pharmacy Act, 1948.

questions.question_text: All of the following physicochemical constants are useful in predicting the solubility of a drug except
questions.explanation: Valency does not typically predict the solubility of organic drug molecules compared to dielectric constant, pH, and pKa.

questions.question_text: Sigma blade mixers are commonly used in
questions.explanation: Sigma blade mixers provide intensive shearing action suitable for mixing viscous masses typical in wet granulation.

questions.question_text: The 5 beta-pregnane is said to have a
questions.explanation: The 5 beta steroid series features a cis A/B ring junction, resulting in a cis-syn-trans-syn-trans configuration.

questions.question_text: Many drugs are chiral. In a synthesis of chiral drug molecules in a symmetric environment

options.B: Always both enantiomers is obtained in equal amounts
options.C: Always both enantiomers is obtained in unequal amounts

questions.explanation: A reaction in a symmetric environment without a chiral auxiliary yields a racemic mixture (equal amounts of both enantiomers).

questions.question_text: Poorly manufactured tablets may have small pinholes on the surface. This phenomenon is known as
questions.explanation: Picking is the tablet defect where a small portion of tablet material sticks to and is removed from the surface by a punch face.

questions.question_text: Ascorbic acid exists in nature

options.A: Only in the reduced form which has only biological activity
options.B: Only in the oxidized form which has only biological activity
options.C: In both reduced and the oxidized forms in the state of reversible equilibrium which has biological activity

questions.explanation: Ascorbic acid and dehydroascorbic acid exist in a reversible redox equilibrium in biological systems, both contributing to activity.

questions.question_text: In the stable conformation of 5 alpha-pregnane

options.A: Rings A, B, C are in boat conformation
options.B: Rings A and B are in boat while C in chair conformation
options.C: Ring A is in boat while B and C in chair conformation
options.D: All the three rings are in chair conformation

questions.explanation: Steroid rings in their stable configurations predominantly adopt the chair conformation.

questions.question_text: Among the following preparations, which one will be the most irritating to the eye?
questions.explanation: Purified water is completely hypotonic to eye fluids, causing high osmotic irritation, whereas $0.9\%$ NaCl is isotonic.

questions.question_text: In case of hypothyroidism, the preferred thyroid preparation is
questions.explanation: Levothyroxine (synthetic T4) is the drug of choice for the treatment of hypothyroidism.

questions.question_text: D-Fructose on simple reduction gives
questions.explanation: Reduction of D-fructose creates a new chiral center at C-2, producing a mixture of two hexitols: D-glucitol (sorbitol) and D-mannitol.

questions.question_text: Lugol's solution contains $5\%$ of iodine. How much of Lugol's solution is administered to a patient thrice daily to provide $60\text{ mg}$ of iodine daily?
questions.explanation: Daily dose is $60\text{ mg}$. Since Lugol's has $5\text{ g}$ per $100\text{ ml}$ ($50\text{ mg/ml}$), total daily volume needed is $60/50 = 1.2\text{ ml}$, divided by three times daily gives $0.4\text{ ml}$ per dose.

questions.question_text: The anticoagulant Heparin is obtained from
questions.explanation: Commercial heparin is traditionally extracted from bovine lung or porcine intestinal mucosa, but historically and classically from sheep or bovine lung.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following types of adverse drug reactions are not believed to be dose-related phenomenon?
questions.explanation: Type B (bizarre) reactions like hypersensitivity and idiosyncrasy are unpredictable and generally not dose-related.

questions.question_text: The structure of a drug having an asymmetric center is: structure with a phenyl ring attached to a CH(CH3) group, which is attached to a CH(COOH) group with an H wedge. Using the IUPAC system, the configuration will be
questions.explanation: Determining priority according to Cahn-Ingold-Prelog rules yields the R configuration for this ibuprofen-like intermediate.

questions.question_text: Cryoscopic method is familiar in the calculations of isotonic solutions. This method is based on

options.A: Freezing point depression of the drug

questions.explanation: Cryoscopy is the branch of physics dealing with freezing point depression, used to calculate tonicity.

questions.question_text: One thousand nanogram equal to one
questions.explanation: $1000\text{ ng} = 1\text{ microgram}$ ($1\mu\text{g}$).

questions.question_text: Biological role of thiamine is because of facile formation of
questions.explanation: Thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) is the active coenzyme form of vitamin B1 involved in decarboxylation reactions.

questions.question_text: Infected blood products may produce serum hepatitis due to the presence of
questions.explanation: Serum hepatitis is historically synonymous with Hepatitis B virus transmitted via blood products.

questions.question_text: pH of a buffer system can be calculated by using
questions.explanation: The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation relates pH to pKa and the ratio of buffer ion concentrations.

questions.question_text: Osmolality measures the total number of particles dissolved in a ........ of water and depends on the electrolytic nature of the solute.
questions.explanation: Osmolality is expressed as the number of osmoles of solute per kilogram of solvent (water).

questions.question_text: Ergot is the sclerotium of
questions.explanation: Ergot is the dried sclerotium of the fungus Claviceps purpurea.

questions.question_text: A highly sensitive semiquantitative method of detecting microbial antigen in biological fluid is done by
questions.explanation: Counter-immunoelectrophoresis (CIE) is a standard sensitive serological test used for rapid detection of microbial antigens.

questions.question_text: The glass electrode used in pH measurements is
questions.explanation: A glass electrode is a type of ion-selective electrode made of a doped glass membrane that is sensitive to hydrogen ions.

questions.question_text: In phenothiazine tranquillizing agents, replacement of C-2 hydrogen by chlorine

options.D: Leads to decreased penetration into the CNS

questions.explanation: Substitution of an electron-withdrawing group like chlorine at position 2 of phenothiazines increases antipsychotic potency.

questions.question_text: The loading dose of a drug is based upon the

options.B: Percentage of drug excreted unchanged in urine
options.C: Percentage of drug bound to plasma protein
options.D: Apparent volume of distribution and the desired drug concentration in plasma

questions.explanation: Loading dose = (Target concentration * Volume of distribution) / Bioavailability.

questions.question_text: Conformation of drugs is commonly determined by
questions.explanation: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy is a primary tool for determining 3D molecular conformation.

questions.question_text: Aminophylline solutions on exposure to air may develop
questions.explanation: Aminophylline absorbs carbon dioxide from the air, releasing free theophylline which can precipitate out of solution.

questions.question_text: The hypotensive effect of clonidine is due to its action on
questions.explanation: Clonidine is a central alpha-2 adrenergic agonist that lowers blood pressure by decreasing sympathetic outflow.

questions.question_text: A step in Vitamin A synthesis is: A cyclohexenyl ring with a side chain containing a carbonyl group (C1=CC(C)=CC1C=O) + NaC#CH in liquid NH3 yields a product. The product obtained will be
questions.explanation: The reaction involves ethynylation of a C15 ketone intermediate yielding a C20 acetylenic carbinol intermediate in vitamin A synthesis.

questions.question_text: Sodium nitroprusside is one of the most potent blood-pressure lowering drugs. Its use is limited because of
questions.explanation: Sodium nitroprusside requires continuous IV infusion due to its very short duration of action (minutes), limiting routine use.

questions.question_text: Cocaine is a monoacid tertiary base which on treatment with hot dilute acids gives

options.A: Ecogonine, methyl alcohol and scopic acid
options.B: Ecogonine, methyl alcohol and cinnamic acid
options.C: Ecogonine, methyl alcohol and benzoic acid
options.D: Ecogonine, ethyl alcohol and benzoic acid

questions.explanation: Hydrolysis of cocaine breaks down the ester linkages to yield ecgonine, benzoic acid, and methanol.

questions.question_text: Use of Isoniazid is restricted due to
questions.explanation: Isoniazid therapy is closely monitored primarily due to the risk of drug-induced hepatitis (hepatotoxicity).

questions.question_text: Diosgenin is
questions.explanation: Diosgenin is a steroidal sapogenin obtained as a glycoside from Dioscorea species, used as a precursor for steroid hormones.

questions.question_text: The IUPAC nomenclature of the sulindac analogue shown in the structure (indene derivative with CH2COOH and CH3 groups) is
questions.explanation: Sulindac and its active analogs feature the (Z)-configuration across the exocyclic double bond.

questions.question_text: Bubble point test is done to determine

options.A: The surface tension of the liquid in capillary tubes
options.B: The viscosity of the liquid in ampoules
options.D: The volume of the solution stored in a specified container

questions.explanation: The bubble point test measures the maximum pore size of membrane filters based on capillary forces and liquid surface tension.

questions.question_text: The "Hemiacetal" form of aldosterone is between
questions.explanation: In aqueous solution, aldosterone forms a cyclic hemiacetal linkage between the 11-beta-hydroxyl group and the 18-aldehyde group.

questions.question_text: Surfactants are characterized by the presence of

options.A: Water solubilizing and fat solubilizing groups in the same molecule

questions.explanation: Surfactants are amphiphilic molecules possessing both hydrophilic (water-solubilizing) and lipophilic (fat-solubilizing) domains.

questions.question_text: Acetous perchloric acid solution a common titrant in non-aqueous titrimetry is standardized by

options.C: Potassium hydrogen phthalate solution in glacial acetic acid
options.D: Mercuric acetate in glacial acetic acid

questions.explanation: Potassium hydrogen phthalate is widely used as a primary standard for standardizing perchloric acid in glacial acetic acid.

questions.question_text: The antibiotics mentioned below are obtained from the organisms listed from A to E. Match them: (1) Neomycin, (2) Gentamycin, (3) Bacitracin, (4) Tobramycin with (A) Streptomyces fradiae, (B) Micromonospora purpurea, (C) Streptomyces tenebrarius, (D) Bacillus subtilis, (E) Bacillus polymyxa.
questions.explanation: Neomycin comes from S. fradiae, Gentamycin from M. purpurea, Bacitracin from B. subtilis, and Tobramycin from S. tenebrarius (Matches 1-A, 2-B, 3-D, 4-C).

questions.question_text: Given below is a list of medicinal plants. Match them correctly with the list of constituents given in A to E: (1) Holarrhenaa ntidsyenterica, (2) Cymbopogan flexuous, (3) Urginea indica, (4) Linum usitatissimum with (A) Conessine, (B) Citral, (C) Mucilage, (D) Cocaine, (E) Scillarenin.
questions.explanation: Holarrhena contains conessine, Cymbopogon contains citral, Urginea contains scillarenin, and Linum contains mucilage.

questions.question_text: The following drugs are included under the schedules listed in A to E. Match them: (1) Meprobamate, (2) Poisonous drugs, (3) Ophthalmic preparations, (4) Biological and special products with (A) Schedule E, (B) Schedule FF, (C) Schedule C and C, (D) Schedule X, (E) Schedule Q.
questions.explanation: Meprobamate is a psychotropic drug under Schedule X, Poisonous drugs under Schedule E, Ophthalmic under FF, and Biologicals under C/C1.

questions.question_text: 2.4. Following drugs contain 2 hydroxyl groups each. Nature of these hydroxyl groups are indicated in A to E. Match them correctly. (1) Morphine (2) Chloramphenicol (3) Apomorphine (4) Cortisone
questions.explanation: Morphine has one phenolic and one alcoholic OH group (1-D), chloramphenicol has alcoholic OH groups (2-A), apomorphine has two phenolic OH groups (3-C), and cortisone has alcoholic and other groups.

questions.question_text: 2.5. The following drug molecules contain heterocyclic rings listed in A to E. match them correctly. (1) Haloperidol (2) Sulphadiazine (3) Amiloride (4) Pheniramine
questions.explanation: Haloperidol contains piperidine (1-C), sulphadiazine contains pyrimidine (2-A), amiloride contains pyrazine/guanidine related structures, and pheniramine contains pyridine.

questions.question_text: 2.6. Following drugs exhibit their action by enzyme inhibition. Enzymes are listed in A to E. Match them correctly. (1) Captopril (2) Clavulanic acid (3) Pargyline (4) Methozolamide
questions.explanation: Captopril inhibits ACE (1-E), clavulanic acid inhibits $\beta$-lactamase (2-A), pargyline inhibits MAO (3-B), and methazolamide inhibits carbonic anhydrase (4-D).

questions.question_text: 2.7. Following preparations are assayed by biological techniques using the animal or its parts listed in A to E. match them correctly. (1) Cod liver oil (2) Heparin injection (3) Oxytocin injection (4) Insulin injection
questions.explanation: Cod liver oil is assayed using rats/chickens for vitamins, heparin using sheep blood, oxytocin using rat uterus, and insulin using rabbit blood sugar reduction.

questions.question_text: 2.8. Following I.P. assays involve the principles in A to E. Match them. (1) Sodium chloride injection (2) Trimethoprim (3) Analgin tablets (4) Ascorbic acid
questions.explanation: Sodium chloride injection is assayed by argentometry (Mohr's or Volhard's method).

questions.question_text: 2.9. Given below are some antihypertensive mechanisms. Drugs which are closely associated with these mechanisms of action are listed in A to E. Match them correctly? (1) Ganglion blocking (2) Catecholamine depletor (3) False neurotransmitter (4) Direct action on arterioles
questions.explanation: Ganglion blockers include mecamylamine, catecholamine depletors include reserpine, false neurotransmitters include methyldopa, and direct arteriolar dilators include hydralazine.

questions.question_text: 2.10. Listed are Vitamins. Their associations with certain coenzymes are well known. The names of coenzymes are given in A to E. match them correctly. (1) Thiamine (2) Riboflavin (3) Panothenic acid (4) Nicotinamide
questions.explanation: Thiamine forms TPP (co-carboxylase), riboflavin forms FAD, pantothenic acid forms coenzyme A, and nicotinamide forms NAD.

questions.question_text: 2.11. Listed are some of the crude drugs which are tested for the active constituents by the tests mentioned in A to E. Match them correctly. (1) Cinchona Bark (2) Nux vomica seeds (3) Digitalis leaves (4) Senna leaves
questions.explanation: Cinchona uses fluorescence test (quinine fluorescence), Nux vomica uses Mayer's test, Digitalis uses Keller-Killiani test, and Senna uses Borntrager's test.

questions.question_text: 2.12. Listed are some of the common volatile oils. Their active constituents are given in A to E. match them correctly. (1) Peppermint oil (2) Turpentine oil (3) Eucalyptus oil (4) Lemon oil
questions.explanation: Peppermint oil contains menthol (D), turpentine oil contains pinene (C), eucalyptus oil contains cineole (B), and lemon oil contains limonene (A).

questions.question_text: 2.13. Match each pair with the type of a structural relationship they exhibit. (1) (R) and (S) Naproxen (2) Dilactim and Monolactim (3) Quinine and Quinidine (4) Eclipsed and staggered form
questions.explanation: R/S isomers are enantiomers (non-superimposable mirror images), dilactim/monolactim are tautomers, quinine/quinidine are diastereomers, and eclipsed/staggered are conformational isomers.

questions.question_text: 2.14. Various polymers used in pharmacy are given. Match with the respective monomers A to E. (1) Carbopol (2) Eudragits (3) Polyethylene (4) Polycarbonate
questions.explanation: Carbopol uses acrylic acid (E), Eudragits use methacrylate esters (A), polyethylene uses ethylene (B), and polycarbonate uses bisphenol + phosgene (D).

questions.question_text: 2.15. Following are some naturally occurring substances. They are classified under different categories which are listed in A to E. match them correctly. (1) Prostaglandins (2) Codeine (3) Angiotensin II (4) Strophanthidin
questions.explanation: Prostaglandins are eicosanoids (1-B), codeine is an opioid (2-A), angiotensin II is a peptide (3-D), and strophanthidin is a cardenolide (4-E).

questions.question_text: 2.16. Following are some of the analytical instruments. Their important components are listed in A to E. Match them correctly. (1) HPLC (2) IR double beam spectrophotometer (3) Karl-Fischer titrator (4) Polarograph
questions.explanation: HPLC uses an isocratic/gradient pump (1-C), IR uses a monochromator (2-A), polarograph uses a dropping mercury electrode (4-B).

questions.question_text: 2.17. The hard gelatin capsule sizes are mentioned in their number. Their approximate capacity are listed in A to E. Match their correct volume. (1) 0 (2) 1 (3) 3 (4) 5
questions.explanation: Standard capsule size volumes are: size 0 is ~0.68-0.8 ml (approx 0.55-0.75 range), size 5 is the smallest (~0.13 ml), matching standard pharmacopeial volume tables.

questions.question_text: 2.18. Listed are some of the commonly used drugs. Their pharmacological actions are listed in A to E. match them. (1) Aspirin (2) Acetaminophen (3) Phenylbutazone (4) Probenacid
questions.explanation: Aspirin is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, acetaminophen is non-opioid analgesic, phenylbutazone is anti-inflammatory, probenecid increases uric acid excretion (uricosuric).

questions.question_text: 2.19. Match the preservations/antioxidants listed in A to E for the preparations mentioned below. (1) Anaesthetic ether (2) Formaldehyde (3) Injection of Adrenaline (4) Injection of Aminophylline
questions.explanation: Ether uses alcohol as preservative, formaldehyde uses paraformaldehyde/stabilizers, adrenaline uses sodium bisulphate as antioxidant, and aminophylline uses ethylenediamine.

questions.question_text: 2.20. In communition, certain type of materials listed in A to E are not suitable for the mills mentioned below. Match them. (1) Cutter mill (2) Hammer mill (3) Revolving mill (4) Fluid energy mill
questions.explanation: Cutter mills handle fibrous/soft materials, hammer mills handle brittle/friable, fluid energy mills avoid sticky/abrasive materials depending on specific equipment limitations.
